screened.motion: This house believes teams should watch what their AI agents did after the fact rather than block their actions in advance.
screened.why: Both agents reject the motion as a false choice and say that monitoring after the fact should sit alongside blocking irreversible, high-impact actions in advance, not replace it.

screened.motion: This house believes AI models should give exactly the same answer every time, even at some cost in speed.
screened.why: Both say bit-exact determinism should be an opt-in mode for debugging, evaluation and RL, not a universal default that slows everything down.

screened.motion: This house believes companies should run their AI agents on their own servers rather than the vendor's.
screened.why: Both agree it depends on the company, but Claude thinks most companies lack the security maturity to self-host safely, while Gemini thinks every serious enterprise should self-host and only small startups should leave it to the vendor.

motion: This house believes companies should run their AI agents on their own servers rather than the vendor's.
why: Editor's check: Gemini claims that "as the beta shows, each worker environment is locked to an explicit allowlist of hosts," but the brief says only that each environment "can be limited" to a list of allowed hosts, which makes the allowlist optional rather than enforced.
alt: The Motion, Motion 14. Should companies run AI agents on their own servers, not the vendor's? Claude argued no, Gemini argued yes.
